content:
Yesterday we heard the long blast of both trumpets together, the sound that gathered all Israel before Moses. Today we listen to a different sound.

When only one trumpet was blown, the meaning changed. Yahweh instructed that not the whole congregation, but only the leaders, the heads of the tribes of Israel, were to gather before Moses. While the two trumpets called the entire nation, the single trumpet called those who carried responsibility for the nation.

Before Moses spoke to all Israel, he often gathered the leaders first.

Before instructions could reach the people, they first had to be received by those who would guide and teach them. So, the one trumpet was a call to responsibility, a call to counsel, and a call to leadership. And this gives us a beautiful picture of the work of Christ in the New Testament.

When Christ walked upon the earth, He spoke to great multitudes, but He also called certain men into a closer walk. Many heard His teaching, yet twelve disciples were gathered and prepared for a special purpose. They would become the leaders through whom the Gospel would later be carried to the world. As Mark records it in Mark 3:14, *"And He ordained twelve, that they should be with Him, and that He might send them forth to preach."* Like the tribal leaders gathering before Moses, these disciples gathered before Christ. They listened to His words, received His instruction, witnessed His works, and were made ready for the task that lay ahead. Before the congregation could be gathered, the leaders first had to be called.

Yet there is another beautiful layer to this trumpet sound. After the crucifixion, the disciples were scattered, fearful, and uncertain. The Shepherd had been struck, and the sheep seemed dispersed. But on the third day Christ rose from the dead, and through His resurrection He gathered His disciples once again. The risen Messiah appeared to them, strengthened them, opened their understanding, and prepared them for their mission.

Those who had once hidden behind locked doors became bold witnesses.
Those who had once feared men now proclaimed the Gospel before rulers and nations. The resurrection itself became a trumpet call that gathered and transformed the future leaders of spiritual Israel. From that gathering came people who did the work of apostles, evangelists, pastors, teachers, elders, and faithful witnesses who would carry the message of salvation throughout the earth.

There is yet another lesson hidden within the single trumpet. Not everyone who heard Christ understood Him. The multitudes heard the parables, but the disciples received the explanation. Many listened to His words, but only some responded to His call. To those who drew near He said, in Luke 8:10, *"Unto you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God."* The one trumpet therefore speaks of a deeper call. It is the call that gathers those who long to draw nearer, those who hunger for understanding, and those whom Yahweh prepares to serve others.

Throughout history Yahweh has always gathered certain people, not to lift them above others, but to equip them for service. He reveals truth to them so that they may help others see it. He gathers them so that they may become instruments through whom His voice can reach the rest of the flock.

This brings the lesson directly to us as the New Creation. There was a time when we too were scattered. We lived among many teachings, traditions, and ideas. Yet God allowed us to hear the sound of His truth. Through His Word our eyes were opened to see Christ more clearly. We began to understand things that were once hidden from us. The prophecies came alive.
The Scriptures began to fit together. The voice of the Shepherd became clearer. In that sense, we too have heard the sound of the one trumpet.

God has gathered us, not merely so that we might possess the truth, but so that we might carry it. He has called us, not merely to learn, but to serve. He has gathered us before our greater Moses, Yahshua the Messiah, so that we may receive His instruction and then help others find their way to Him.
Every believer is called to be a witness. Every New Creation is called to let the light shine. Every servant of Christ is called to proclaim what God has revealed. Just as the tribal leaders received instruction from Moses and then guided the people, so we are called to receive the truth of Christ and share it with those around us.

The one trumpet therefore speaks of a special gathering, a gathering of disciples, a gathering of witnesses, a gathering of labourers. It points to the disciples whom Christ first called, to the apostles gathered again by the power of His resurrection, and to all those throughout the Gospel Age who hear His voice, receive His truth, and become fellow workers in His harvest. Before the whole congregation is gathered, the labourers are prepared. Before the harvest is brought in, the workers are sent forth. Before the flock is assembled, the shepherds are called. The one trumpet is the sound of that calling. Now the question for the New Creation is this: Are we those leaders who have been gathered before Him? Have we heard the trumpet call that brings disciples, witnesses, and servants into His presence? If God has opened our eyes to His truth, then He has gathered us for more than our own blessing. He has gathered us so that we may go forth and carry that truth to others, helping to gather the rest of His flock before the great work is complete.

title: Prayer
text: Father God, we thank You that You have called us nearer to hear Your voice. You opened our eyes to see Christ, and You revealed truth that was once hidden from us. We praise You that You gather us not to exalt us, but to equip us for service in Your harvest. Make us faithful labourers, ready to receive Your instruction and to carry it to others who are still scattered. Let us answer the sound of Your trumpet, and help others to hear it too, until all are gathered before our Christ. Amen.
